name: Pending Failing Settlement 1 Code
definition: Specifies the reason the transaction/instruction is pending failing settlement, and the settlement at the instruction settlement date is no longer possible.

AWMO.name: Awaiting Money
AWMO.definition: Securities have been delivered, but the money is still expected from the counterparty.

AWSH.name: Awaiting Securities From Counterparty
AWSH.definition: Securities have not yet been received from the counterparty. If the settlement instruction was a received against payment, the cash has been delivered.

DOCY.name: Awaiting Documents Or Endorsements From You
DOCY.definition: Awaiting documents or endorsements from you.

CLAT.name: Counterparty Too Late For Settlement
CLAT.definition: Counterparty's instruction was too late for settlement, (that is, received too late, matching, or settlement problems were solved too late).

MINO.name: Minimum Settlement Amount
MINO.definition: Securities quantity is lower than the minimum existing settlement quantity for the instructed financial instrument.

PHSE.name: Physical Delivery Delay
PHSE.definition: Settlement is physical, and there is a delay in the delivery of the securities.

SBLO.name: Securities Blocked
SBLO.definition: Securities are blocked, for example, because of a corporate action event or re-alignment.

DKNY.name: Counterparty Returned Securities
DKNY.definition: Counterparty has returned, refused, or does not recognize the securities.

LACK.name: Lack Of Securities
LACK.definition: Insufficient deliverable securities in your account.

LATE.name: Too Late For Settlement
LATE.definition: Settlement instruction was too late for settlement, that is, received too late, matching, or settlement problems were solved too late.

CANR.name: Cancellation Confirmation Request
CANR.definition: Transaction suspended. Because the suspension period is finished, the cancellation or confirmation of instructions is required.

MLAT.name: Money Too Late For Settlement
MLAT.definition: Payment for a buy of securities was received after the cut-off time for completing the settlement on a same day basis.

OBJT.name: Under Objection
OBJT.definition: Securities are stolen, in dispute, and under objection.

DOCC.name: Awaiting Documents Or Endorsements From Counterparty
DOCC.definition: Awaiting documents or endorsements from the counterparty.

BLOC.name: Account Blocked
BLOC.definition: Account is blocked, so no instruction can settle.

CHAS.name: Enquiry Sent
CHAS.definition: Enquiry/chaser sent to the agent or depository.

NEWI.name: New Issues
NEWI.definition: Securities are new issues, and not yet available/tradeable.

CLAC.name: Counterparty Insufficient Securities
CLAC.definition: Insufficient deliverable securities in the counterparty's account, or counterparty does not hold the securities.

COLL.name: Securities Pledged As Collateral
COLL.definition: Securities are not deliverable as they are pledged as collateral.

DEPO.name: Refused Deposit For Issue Of Depositary Receipts
DEPO.definition: Deposit of shares for the issuance of a depositary receipt has been refused. The allotment for depositary receipts granted by the issuer would be exceeded by the transaction.

FLIM.name: Maximum Foreign Limit Reached
FLIM.definition: Insufficient deliverable securities in your account, as maximum foreign limit has been reached.

NOFX.name: No Foreign Exchange Instruction
NOFX.definition: A foreign exchange instruction from you is missing.

INCA.name: Income Adjustement Required
INCA.definition: Securities require income adjustment, that is, dividend or interest.

BYIY.name: Buy In Procedure
BYIY.definition: A buy-in procedure has started on the market, on your behalf, if your instruction is a receipt, or on behalf of the counterparty if the instruction is a delivery.

CAIS.name: Awaiting Securities
CAIS.definition: Awaiting securities from a corporate action issue or other procedure(s), for example, conversion, dematerialisation, exchange, registration, stamping, and splitting.

LALO.name: Securities Loaned Out
LALO.definition: Insufficient deliverable securities in your account as securities are loaned out.

NCON.name: Confirmation Not Received
NCON.definition: Settlement confirmation has not yet been received.

YCOL.name: Collateral Shortage
YCOL.definition: Not enough collateral in your account to execute the instruction.

REFS.name: Not In Good Order
REFS.definition: Delivery/receipt is refused because the physical securities are not in good order.

SDUT.name: Lack Of Stamp Duty Information
SDUT.definition: Instruction is failing since stamp duty information is missing.

CYCL.name: Awaiting Next Settlement Cycle
CYCL.definition: Your instruction is confirmed in the local market, but is ready for settlement at the next settlement cycle.

BATC.name: Processing Batch Difference
BATC.definition: Processing batch differs in the counterparty's instruction, for example, day time/real time vs overnight.

GUAD.name: Guaranteed Delivery Indicator Difference
GUAD.definition: Guaranteed delivery indicator differs in the counterparty's instruction.

PREA.name: Preadvice Instructed
PREA.definition: Instruction is a preadvice, that is, matching only.

CPEC.name: Counterparty In Receivership
CPEC.definition: Counterparty is in receivership, that is, a form of bankruptcy.

MUNO.name: Multiple Settlement Amount
MUNO.definition: Amount is not a multiple of an existing settlement amount lot for the instructed financial instrument.
